0/1:
**The Sea**

Salt on the wind, a long gray swell,
the tide comes in and counts the shells
it borrowed from the shore — and takes
them back, and takes them back, and takes
the footprints of our footprints too.

Nothing here is finished. Nothing holds.
The wave lifts, leans, and lets it go.
And I stand watching, thinking: this
is all the sea has ever wanted —
to be water, and to leave.

0/2:
**The Sea**

The sea does not ask,
and never answers —
it only keeps
its long blue secret.

Waves come in like letters
with no signature,
folding themselves
against the shore, then leaving.

Salt on my tongue,
wind in the rigging of my hair —
I have been walking toward it
since before I had a name.

And when the tide goes out,
it takes a little of me
with it,
the way a friend
borrows
